title: Porter-Braised Chuck with Caramelized Onion Gravy
description: Lean chuck shoulder braises in hickory broth and finishes in a smooth gravy made from golden onions and porter.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly
Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: lean boneless beef chuck shoulder roast
ingredients.note: Choose the lean shoulder or clod; remove external fat and thick seams before weighing.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: small yellow onion
ingredients.note: Slice paper-thin; caramelize completely before adding to the gravy.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with hickory pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {mustard} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Portion the chuck
steps.text: Cut {beef} across the grain into 1-inch pieces, removing any seams of fat you uncover.

steps.title: Seal the pot
steps.text: Tuck the pieces into the broth. Keep them at least halfway submerged, adding {topup} if necessary. Fit the lid immediately. No stall-wrap temperature applies.

steps.title: Braise until tender
steps.text: Cook covered at 300°F for 1 3/4 to 2 3/4 hours. Start testing at about 195°F and continue until a fork turns easily in several pieces.

steps.title: Caramelize the onion
steps.text: While the beef cooks, soften {onion} in {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low for 25–35 minutes, stirring and adding splashes of {topup} as needed, until completely soft and deep gold.

steps.title: Reduce the porter
steps.text: Pour {porter} into the caramelized onion and simmer for 3–5 minutes until a thin syrup clings to the pan.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered chuck off heat for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Keep the beef moist
steps.text: Move the beef to a covered bowl with a little braising liquid.

steps.title: Puree the onions
steps.text: Add 1 1/2 cups skimmed braising liquid to the onions, topping up with {topup} if needed. Blend in a deep heatproof jug with an immersion blender until smooth and return the gravy to the HexClad.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} until completely smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the beef
steps.text: Break the chuck into short, tender pieces with a fork and fold them into the onion gravy.

notes: Make ahead: Caramelize the onions a day in advance. Option A uses porter. For an alcohol-free or gentler Option B, replace the beer with an equal volume of plain low-sodium beef broth. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 245 kcal, 32.2 g protein, 5.4 g total carbohydrate, 9.9 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 148 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth. Calories include all the measured alcohol before simmering.
